 Plot leaks for One Piece Chapter 1198 describe Killingham fleeing Sanji, Imu defeating Loki, and Luffy gaining a new form.
 1 / 6 List slides One Piece Chapter 1198: 4 plot leaks, from Imu's third form to Luffy's apparent exit List slides Previous Start over By Cris Tolomia · Updated November 5, 2026 Add QZ to Google Illustration: Quartz
 A manga reader who opens a social feed in the days before a new chapter can stumble into its biggest moments without warning. Spoilers spread online before each new installment lands, and a series with a cast as crowded as One Piece gives them plenty to reveal. A single leaked page can reshape how fans read the arc that follows. Some readers chase every scrap of early information. Others mute keywords and avoid forums until the chapter itself arrives. Both camps feel the pull, and anyone who follows the saga has to decide how much to learn and when. Chapter 1198 has reached that stage, with plot details circulating ahead of its debut.
 Advance synopses carry built-in uncertainty. They surface before the publisher puts out the chapter, and they can arrive without any named origin, which leaves readers no way to check them against the finished pages. A pronoun can point to the wrong character. A short description can blur who acts and who reacts. A scene that sounds decisive in a synopsis can unfold in a different way once the artwork appears. Fans who treat these unverified reports as settled fact risk building expectations on sand. A safer habit holds each reported event as provisional until the published chapter confirms or corrects it. The previews still deserve attention, because they hint at where the narrative is heading and which characters will carry its next stretch.
 Yahoo Entertainment published a spoiler roundup by Ishita Verma on Nov. 4, 2026, gathering online leaks for Chapter 1198 of the One Piece manga. The leaks give the chapter a title, "The Island of Monsters." Verma's article rests on anonymous accounts alone. It identifies no leaker, no raw scan, and no release date for the chapter. Verma recaps the previous chapter in one line, then works through the action in three brief headed sections. Each of the four developments below traces to those uncredited sources. Treat every one as a leak until the chapter reaches readers.
 Killingham flees Sanji after losing his armor 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Killingham spends the first scene of Chapter 1198 running from Sanji, according to the plot leaks, after the Straw Hat's kick breaks his armor apart. The shattered armor decides the encounter. Once Sanji's strike strips away his protection, Killingham gives up the fight and bolts.
 The roundup gives this getaway pride of place. Verma lists it ahead of every other leaked event, and the chase opens the chapter itself. Readers learn how Sanji's clash ends before they see anything of the larger battle unfolding elsewhere.
 The roundup likens Killingham's retreat to Saint Sommers running from Zoro. The parallel pairs Sanji with Zoro, two Straw Hats who each leave an opponent scrambling for safety. It also casts Killingham's collapse as a repeat of an earlier pattern, in which an enemy facing a Straw Hat chooses flight once the fight turns against him.
 Mid-flight, Killingham picks up the haki of Imu, the World Government leader, the spoilers report. The detail ties the chapter's opening thread to Imu, who sits at the center of the next leaked events. Killingham slips away from one danger and stumbles into the presence of a far greater one.
 The leaks leave several questions open. They do not say whether Sanji gives chase, where Killingham heads, or how he responds once he senses Imu. Until the published chapter appears, nobody can say whether the run ends in escape or in a confrontation with the World Government leader.
 Loki reels as Luffy appears to leave the battlefield 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Loki, the Prince of Elbaph, ends up stunned in the leaked Chapter 1198 after he remarks that Luffy seems to have left the battlefield. The plot summary never describes a confirmed exit. It treats Luffy's absence as an impression, and the prince is the one who voices it.
 The roundup hedges as well. Its section heading says Luffy has "reportedly" left the battlefield. The article's own framing marks the departure as unverified, a layer of doubt beyond the uncertainty that surrounds any leak.
 Imu's third form sets the scene moments before Loki speaks. The World Government leader shifts into a shape with a stretched torso, huge horns, and a long neck, according to the leaks. Verma's write-up places this change ahead of Loki's observation, pairing Imu's altered body with the sudden disappearance of Luffy.
 The timing sharpens Loki's shock. Luffy appears to vanish in the same stretch of the chapter where Imu escalates, and Loki is the character the leaks show registering it.
 Luffy's whereabouts stay unresolved in this passage. The leaked account offers no word on where he went or why he left, and it records nothing he does next. Readers get Loki's comment and the jolt it produces, nothing more.
 Loki's alarm hinges on an event the source never explains, and only the published chapter can confirm whether his reading of the field holds.
 Imu crushes Loki with a single attack 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Imu, the World Government leader, takes down Loki with one attack, according to the plot leaks for Chapter 1198. The Prince of Elbaph falls without surrendering the information Imu demands.
 Elbaph's ancient technology sits at the center of the confrontation. Imu presses Loki for details about what Elbaph keeps and chooses to question the prince before striking. The order of events shows the technology holds Imu's interest. Loki gives nothing away. He refuses to utter a word on the subject.
 The roundup never describes the technology itself. Readers learn only that Elbaph possesses it and that Imu wants it. Its nature and purpose stay out of the synopsis, just as Loki withholds them from his questioner.
 Imu's compliment comes before the decisive blow. Imu acknowledges Loki's strength in the reported exchange, then ends the clash with a single strike. Praise and outcome, taken together, show Imu treating Loki as a worthy opponent and overpowering him anyway. The respect buys Loki no reprieve.
 Loki's silence outlasts his resistance. Nothing in the early reports shows Imu learning what Elbaph holds. The secret remains beyond Imu's reach even after the prince goes down. The World Government leader walks away with a win in combat and no answer to the question that started the encounter.
 Luffy gains a new Zoan-type form 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Luffy takes on a new Zoan-type form in the Chapter 1198 plot leaks, turning up on the roof of a house in the village in a guise the summary calls mysterious. The spoilers give him black hair, a tail, fangs, and an ape-like nose. The tail and the nose give the form a beastly cast that suits Gaban's Zoan-type label.
 Gaban supplies the label after he and Usopp ask where Luffy has gone. Their question echoes Loki's earlier surprise at the same absence, and three characters end up puzzling over one disappearance. Gaban's answer speaks to what Luffy has become. The leaks then settle where he is by placing him on that rooftop.
 Gaban and Usopp talk while a separate scene plays out in the same section. The roundup opens that section with Imu pressing Loki about Elbaph's ancient technology before defeating him. Luffy misses the whole stretch in which the Prince of Elbaph loses his fight.
 A rain God bears the brunt of the new form. Luffy spots her, leaps onto her without pause, and bites her. The bite makes her explode. She is the only opponent the leaks show Luffy facing in the chapter. The leaks give no motive for the assault, and they say nothing about who the rain God is or what she was doing before Luffy struck.
 Beyond Gaban's Zoan-type call, the leaks describe how the form looks and show it at work. The fangs on the spoilers' list find a use in the bite, and one bite proves enough to blow apart a god. Loki fell to a single strike from Imu earlier in the chapter, and Luffy now ends an encounter of his own with one move.
 The leaks never name the animal behind the form or say how Luffy acquired it. Readers can picture the new form and its first strike, yet the published pages must supply its origin.
